clippings.speaker: Denis Villeneuve
clippings.quote: I remember having dinner alone with Hans, it was his birthday and we were alone in a Montreal restaurant. And I said Hans,  'I would love you to do the dual scoring' and he said, 'Denis this is my oldest dream. And I will say yes.' But he said, 'I'm just afraid that maybe it's a very dangerous idea to tackle your oldest dream. But let's try it.'
clippings.title: Interview: Denis Villeneuve Talks 'Dune', Assembling The Cast, Hans Zimmer's Score, Hopes For Part Two & More
clippings.context: Roundtable interview ahead of Dune's release, recalling how he asked Zimmer to score it.

clippings.speaker: Denis Villeneuve
clippings.quote: You know, when you put Hans Zimmer on the score, it always takes a lot of space. So there was a way to try and find a balance with sound design, and it was a beautiful artistic dance between the sound and music.
clippings.title: Interview: Denis Villeneuve Talks 'Dune', Assembling The Cast, Hans Zimmer's Score, Hopes For Part Two & More
clippings.context: Same roundtable, on blending Zimmer's music with the film's sound design.

clippings.speaker: Denis Villeneuve
clippings.quote: didn't hear from Hans for a long time. He took a long time to experiment." Then, during editing, "we started receiving tons of music for weeks. It was like a big creative rush. It became a storm. When the movie was totally finished, Hans was still sending me music.
clippings.title: Hans Zimmer on 'Dune' Score's Electronic Textures and Made-Up Language
clippings.context: Villeneuve speaking to Variety about how Zimmer's Dune score arrived during editing.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: But when Denis very quietly asked me, there was something in the way he said had I ever read the book, that I knew he had made the same movie in his head that I was making in my head. And correct me if I'm wrong, but I think part of our process was that whenever we discussed things somehow, it was a full on conclusion that we felt the same way about certain things.
clippings.title: On The Scene: Denis Villeneuve & Hans Zimmer Talk 'Dune' at NYFF Q&A
clippings.context: Joint Q&A with Villeneuve at the New York Film Festival premiere of Dune.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: And I think that it's pretty provocative, let's be honest, it's a pretty provocative score. Thank you Denis for letting me do this.
clippings.title: On The Scene: Denis Villeneuve & Hans Zimmer Talk 'Dune' at NYFF Q&A
clippings.context: Same NYFF Q&A, said to Villeneuve on stage.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: You know those sort of dogs that get really excited? … I became one of those. He [Denis] never let me read the script because he wanted me to stay pure. He wanted one person who was like, I know the book, I know what this is all about, I know what the complications are as well of telling this story.
clippings.title: Hans Zimmer on Unearthing New Sounds for "Dune: Part Two"
clippings.context: MPA's The Credits interview on scoring Dune: Part Two; the article splits the quote with "Zimmer joked."
